title: Four-Port Fault Witness — Longitudinal Momentum Recovery
status: predeclared fault-injection ablation; real-data validation required

faultProtocol.note: Injected faults are artificial and not claims of actual CERN detector failure.

ports.label: ATLAS
ports.softwareFunction: energy E1 and E2 and invariant-mass control

ports.label: LHCb
ports.softwareFunction: reported longitudinal momentum pz1, potentially dropped or corrupted

reconstruction.naiveMissingPolicy: fill missing pz1 with zero; for finite corrupted value, trust corrupted pz1
reconstruction.witnessPolicy: if pz1 missing or |pz1 - pt1*sinh(eta1)| > threshold, use pt1*sinh(eta1); otherwise preserve original pz1
reconstruction.negativeMassSquared: return invalid NaN; do not clamp
reconstruction.operationalGoal: recover known clean four-vector mass calculation under one-field failures, not independent hidden physics

evaluation.split: same deterministic heldout event subset as v8.7
scoreTargets: stored CMS mass M (second consistency reference)
statistics: error wrt clean mass on finite
expectedControls: bias case should be detected when discrepancy above threshold

limits: The fields pt, eta and pz are alternative calculations from the same reconstructed CMS track; they are not independently instrumented detectors.
This test exercises internal data redundancy and synthetic fault repair, not cross-detector recovery or physical particle emergence.
Reference mass M and clean source 4-vector are derived from the same event; scores demonstrate arithmetic consistency, not discovery.
Bias and tolerance are fixed model choices; detection can fail for correlated faults, errors below threshold, or multiple simultaneous faults.
CERN educational data is not suitable for a complete physics analysis.
